newsitem.title: USA: American Eagle Group expects lower revs.
newsitem.headline: American Eagle Group expects lower revs.

text.p: American Eagle Group Inc said on Friday that it expected its revenues and earnings capacity to be "significantly lower" after the sale of its aviation and artisan contractor insurance operations.
The company said it would continue to handle claims on the company's policies that were not included in the sale of those units and to maintain reserves related to those claims.
"Accordingly, the company's revenues and earnings capacity will be significantly lower in the furture," American Eagle Group said in a statement.
It added that financial data on the effect of the transactions will be included in a proxy statement to shareholders to be issued in the second quarter.

The company reported a net loss of $5.7 million in the first quarter of 1997 as compared to a net loss of $2.8 million in the first quarter of 1996. The first quarter of 1997 did not include the effect of any tax benefits, while the first quarter of 1996 included the effect of $1.4 million of tax benefits, American Eagle Group said.
The company also posted a combined ratio of 130.6 percent in the first quarter of 1997, up 14.0 points from 116.6 percent in the year-ago period.
American Eagle Group Inc is an insurance holding company that markets specialized property and casualty coverages in niche markets.
